faqs.question: Is it okay to wish a Hindu colleague Happy Navratri if I'm not Hindu?
faqs.answer: Yes. A plain "Happy Navratri" is the polite default, and research on religious greeting messages finds that standard, familiar wording builds trust rather than sounding lazy. Leave out goddess references unless you know the colleague is observant.

faqs.question: What can I say to a friend who has never heard of Navratri?
faqs.answer: Pair the wish with one sentence of context, such as "It's a nine-night Indian festival honouring the goddess Durga, and in Gujarat people dance garba in big circles." One accurate line is enough; avoid comparing it to Christmas or New Year.

faqs.question: Do all Hindus fast during Navratri?
faqs.answer: No. A 2017 review in the Indian Journal of Endocrinology and Metabolism says Navratri eating patterns have no fixed rule and vary from community to community, from one or two meals a day to fruit and dairy only. Ask whether someone is fasting rather than assuming it.

faqs.question: Should I say Happy Navratri or Happy Durga Puja to a Bengali friend?
faqs.answer: For most Bengali friends the same days are Durga Puja, so "Happy Durga Puja" fits better than garba-themed Navratri lines. If you are unsure, "Happy Navratri and Durga Puja" covers both without being wrong.

faqs.question: Is Navratri the same as Dussehra?
faqs.answer: No. Navratri is the nine nights; Dussehra, also called Vijayadashami, is the day after them. In 2026 Navratri ran 11 to 19 October and Dussehra fell on Tuesday 20 October.

faqs.question: When is Navratri in 2027?
faqs.answer: Sharad Navratri 2027 runs from Thursday 30 September to Friday 8 October, with Dussehra on Saturday 9 October, according to Drik Panchang set to New Delhi. Check the city setting, because some calendars default to a US location.

faqs.question: Why do Ashtami and Navami fall on one day in 2026?
faqs.answer: Hindu festival days follow lunar tithis, which do not line up one-to-one with calendar dates. In 2026 Drik Panchang's New Delhi calendar places both Durga Ashtami and Maha Navami on Monday 19 October, so day-by-day lists that put Ashtami on 18 October are wrong for that year.

faqs.question: Is it too late to send a wish after the first night?
faqs.answer: No. Navratri lasts nine nights, so a wish on night three still arrives during the festival. People tend to act late anyway: in SubhSandesh's nearest festival measurement, 86.1% of Raksha Bandhan pages finished in time were made within 24 hours of the day.

faqs.question: How do I reply when someone wishes me Happy Navratri?
faqs.answer: "Thank you, happy Navratri to you and your family too" works whether or not you celebrate. If you do not celebrate, adding "enjoy the garba" or "enjoy the festival" keeps it warm without claiming a faith you do not hold.

faqs.question: Can I invite a whole group with the Be My Dandiya Partner page?
faqs.answer: No. It is a one-to-one invitation for a love, a crush or a best friend as a garba buddy, ending in a question to one person. For an office or society group, send a plain text wish instead.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Navratri Wishes in English That Work for a Mixed Audience

The safest Navratri wishes in English name the festival, add one plain line saying what it is, and assume nothing about the reader's faith or fast. Below are 27 original wishes in six groups, each with a one-line explainer you can paste for a colleague, an NRI cousin or a friend abroad who has never heard the word. Timing matters as much as wording: on SubhSandesh, 49.4% of 89 Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages were made on the festival day itself (a Raksha Bandhan measurement, used as the nearest analogue, not Navratri data), and 48.3% of all shared pages are opened on a phone.

So write short, and send on the day.

## What is Navratri, in one line a non-Hindu friend will understand?

Navratri is a nine-night Hindu festival honouring the goddess Durga, followed by Dussehra (Vijayadashami), the day that celebrates good defeating evil. Sharad Navratri ran from Sunday 11 October to Monday 19 October 2026, with Dussehra on Tuesday 20 October, per [Drik Panchang's New Delhi calendar for 2026](https://www.drikpanchang.com/navratri/ashwin-shardiya-navratri-dates.html?geoname-id=1261481&year=2026).

In 2027 it runs from Thursday 30 September to Friday 8 October, with Dussehra on Saturday 9 October ([Drik Panchang, 2027](https://www.drikpanchang.com/navratri/ashwin-shardiya-navratri-dates.html?geoname-id=1261481&year=2027)). A spring Navratri also falls in March or April, so check which one a wish list was written for.

It is not practised one way. A [2017 review in the Indian Journal of Endocrinology and Metabolism](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC5240068) notes that people fast and worship the goddess in north India, dance garba and dandiya raas in western India, and follow other local traditions elsewhere.

## 6 groups of English Navratri wishes, each with an explainer

Each group gives an explainer to paste, who it suits, the wishes and one thing to avoid. All 27 lines are original.

### 1. Colleagues, managers and clients

**Explainer to paste:** "Navratri is a nine-night Indian festival of music, dance and family, ending with Dussehra."

**Use it for:** office Slack, email sign-offs, clients.

- "Happy Navratri! Wishing you nine bright evenings and a calm week of work in between them."
- "Happy Navratri to you and your family. I hope the festival brings good food, good music and a little rest."
- "Happy Navratri! May the next nine nights be full of colour, and the deadlines be kind."
- "Warm wishes for Navratri and Dussehra from all of us on the team."

**Avoid:** "May Maa Durga bless you" in a work channel unless you know the person is observant. It reads as presuming their faith.

### 2. Non-Hindu and international friends

**Explainer to paste:** "It's Navratri, nine nights when Hindus honour the goddess Durga, and in Gujarat whole neighbourhoods dance in big circles called garba."

**Use it for:** a friend in Toronto, a neighbour, anyone new to the word.

- "Happy Navratri! It's a nine-night Indian festival, and tonight I'm dancing in a circle with a few hundred strangers. Wish me stamina."
- "Sending you Navratri wishes from my side of the world: nine nights of music, lights and far too many sweets."
- "Happy Navratri! Think of it as nine nights of good overcoming bad, with dancing."
- "You've heard me talk about garba. It starts tonight. Happy Navratri from a very tired pair of feet."

**Avoid:** calling it "Indian Christmas" or "Hindu New Year"; neither is accurate.

### 3. NRI family and elders

**Explainer to paste** (for a partner or child raised abroad): "Navratri is the nine-night festival of the goddess Durga; the family lights a lamp every evening."

**Use it for:** parents in India while you live abroad, or a family group across time zones.

- "Happy Navratri, Ma and Papa. The garba here starts at 8 pm, which is your early morning. Saving you a video."
- "Jai Mata Di! Wishing the whole family strength, health and nine peaceful nights."
- "May Maa Durga keep everyone at home safe and well. Happy Navratri from all of us, even from this far away."
- "Wishing you a blessed Navratri. Call me after the evening puja; I want to see the decorations."

**Avoid:** assuming they are fasting. Ask "Are you keeping the fast this year?" rather than "Hope the fast is going well."

### 4. Friends who play garba

**Explainer to paste:** "Garba is the circle dance of Navratri; dandiya raas is the paired version, danced with sticks."

**Use it for:** your garba group.

- "Happy Navratri! Nine nights, one pair of shoes, no regrets."
- "May your feet keep up with the dhol and your phone survive the circle. Happy Navratri!"
- "Wishing you nine nights of perfect claps, minimal blisters and one photo where nobody blinked."
- "See you in the circle at nine. I'll be the one slightly out of step. Happy Navratri!"
- "Here's to nine nights of dancing like the music will never stop. Happy Navratri, partner."

**Avoid:** garba lines for a Bengali friend whose festival is Durga Puja; say "Happy Durga Puja".

### 5. Short wishes and quotes for status, stories and big groups

**Explainer to paste:** "Navratri: nine nights, one goddess, many ways to celebrate."

**Use it for:** a WhatsApp status, an Instagram story, or a 200-person group.

- "Nine nights of light. Happy Navratri."
- "Courage is a festival too. Happy Navratri."
- "May nine nights bring nine new beginnings."
- "Dance first, sleep after Dussehra."
- "Lamps lit, hearts open. Happy Navratri."
- "Good wins. It just dances on the way."

**Avoid:** long goddess-image forwards in a mixed group; they presume everyone shares the faith.

### 6. Last-night and Dussehra wishes

**Explainer to paste:** "Dussehra, the day after Navratri, marks the victory of good over evil; in 2026 it falls on Tuesday 20 October."

**Use it for:** the final evening and the morning after.

- "The ninth night is here. Thank you for dancing through all of them with me. Happy Navratri."
- "Happy Dussehra! May whatever was weighing on you burn with the effigy tonight."
- "Nine nights done, one fresh start ahead. Happy Vijayadashami."
- "Navratri ends; the good it stood for stays. Happy Dussehra."

**Avoid:** "Happy Dussehra" before the ninth night is over. In 2026 Durga Ashtami and Maha Navami share Monday 19 October, so a forward listing Ashtami on 18 October is wrong for that year.

## When should you send a Navratri wish?

Send on the first evening, and send Dussehra wishes on the morning of the day itself. SubhSandesh has no Navratri timing data yet, so the table uses 89 Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages, a one-day festival. It is direction, not a Navratri rate.

| When the page was built | Share of 89 Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages | Navratri 2026 equivalent | Wish group that fits |
|---|---|---|---|
| On the festival day | 49.4% | Sun 11 Oct, first evening | Groups 1, 2 and 3 |
| The day before | 27.0% | Sat 10 Oct | Groups 3 and 4 |
| Two to three days ahead | 5.6% | Thu 8 to Fri 9 Oct | Group 1, as a planned office note |
| Four or more days ahead | 6.7% | Wed 7 Oct or earlier | Rarely needed |
| After it had passed | 11.2% | Dussehra, Tue 20 Oct | Group 6 |

The habit is last-minute: of the 79 Raksha Bandhan pages finished in time, 86.1% were made within 24 hours of the day. Navratri forgives that, because a missed first evening still leaves eight more nights.

## 5 mistakes that land badly with a mixed audience

**Assuming everyone fasts.** The 2017 endocrinology review states that Navratri eating patterns "have no fixed rule and vary from community to community": some people eat one or two meals, others only fruit, vegetables and dairy. It also explains why fasting is not advisable for some people with diabetes.

**Sending devotion to people who are not religious.** Melanie Barbato's 2023 chapter on [religious greeting messages](https://www.taylorfrancis.com/chapters/edit/10.4324/9781003301271-15/religious-greeting-messages-genre-institutional-communication-melanie-barbato) in the Routledge Handbook of Language and Religion finds festival greetings standardised and repetitive, and argues that familiar patterns build trust. A predictable "Happy Navratri" is the polite default; keep "Jai Mata Di" for people who would say it back. (Only the abstract was read.)

**Forgetting that word choice reads as a stance.** A [2023 paper in Theory and Society](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10238238) recounts Donald Trump vowing to replace the inclusive greeting "happy holidays" with "merry Christmas". Register gets noticed: keep group messages neutral and devotion one-to-one.

**Copying a date list without checking the city.** For 2026, Drik Panchang's New Delhi setting puts Durga Ashtami and Maha Navami on the same day, 19 October. Set the location before pasting a day-by-day goddess list.

**Mixing up festivals.** Navratri is not Diwali, which follows about three weeks later, and Dussehra comes after the nine nights, not at the start.

## Inviting one person to garba: the Be My Dandiya Partner page

For the one person you want beside you in the circle, a text wish undersells it. The [Be My Dandiya Partner invitation](https://subhsandesh.in/dandiya-partner) takes both your names, nine short lines (one for each night), up to six photos, a note, and the night's date, time, venue and dress code.

The recipient clashes dandiya sticks to open an envelope, lights nine diyas round a garbo, plays a short dhol-beat game and picks the colour they will twirl in. The No button twirls away with a new excuse each time and, after five tries, turns into a second Yes; then they can download a 1080×1920 Dandiya Pass, Instagram Story size.

It works for a love, a crush or a best friend as a garba buddy. The interface is in English and opens in any phone or laptop browser, with no app or account.

## When a personal page is the wrong choice

It is a one-to-one invitation, so it is the wrong tool for an office group, a housing-society notice or a 40-person family chat; send a line from group 1 or 5 instead. It does not sell garba passes or find anyone a partner.

For an elder who does not use a smartphone browser, a phone call does more. If the plan is dinner after Dussehra rather than a night in the circle, a [date invitation page](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation) fits better, and the [full SubhSandesh template list](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) covers other occasions.

- Gupta L et al. [Pragmatic dietary advice for diabetes during Navratris](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC5240068). Indian J Endocrinol Metab, January 2017.
- Barbato M. [Religious Greeting Messages as a Genre of Institutional Communication](https://www.taylorfrancis.com/chapters/edit/10.4324/9781003301271-15/religious-greeting-messages-genre-institutional-communication-melanie-barbato). Routledge, 16 November 2023. Abstract only.
- Schwarz O. [Why did Trump call prayers politically correct?](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10238238) Theory and Society, June 2023.

auditReport.honestAssessment: Every top-10 result measured on 12 Oct 2026 (US-served) is weak: Quint pages for Chaitra 2020/2021, a 2024 Leverage Edu list, a 2013 forum thread, an image-download page and scraped mirrors, and all of them assume a devout Hindu recipient. This is the only page that writes for a recipient who may not know the festival, with an explainer per group, verified 2026/2027 dates (including Ashtami and Navami sharing 19 Oct 2026) and first-party timing data, which gives an answer engine something to cite beyond 'more wishes'. It cannot overcome the domain authority of The Quint, and the wish lines themselves are not defensible as data; the timing table is a Raksha Bandhan analogue, not Navratri measurement.
